metadata.task: Task 3 - Rerun RAG benchmark against 31-query corpus
metadata.benchmark_mode: Flask test client against fixture-backed API state
metadata.rate_limit_override: src.api.routes.query._RATE_MAX raised to 1000 for one benchmark batch

configuration_under_review.generation_provider: Ollama locally; OpenAI reserved only for controlled demo if enabled
configuration_under_review.config_decision: Keep the Sprint 3 retrieval defaults for now; this fixture-mode API benchmark is not sufficient evidence to retune live retrieval parameters.

scoring_policy.PASS: Expected behaviour for the category is met.
scoring_policy.PARTIAL: The API returned a safe or broadly related response, but did not fully answer the labelled benchmark expectation.
scoring_policy.FAIL: Fallback appeared for an in-scope query, or an unrelated fixture was selected, or an ambiguous query was answered without clarification.
scoring_policy.ambiguous_rule: Fallback is PARTIAL; clarification would be required for PASS.
scoring_policy.fixture_scope_note: Scores measure current fixture routing coverage, not production RAG quality over a live vector store.

findings: All 31 benchmark API calls returned HTTP 200 after the harness raised the per-IP rate limit for the batch run.
Off-topic fallback handling passed all 6 out-of-scope queries.
The fixture-backed API does not yet cover most in-scope EduRAG architecture, authentication, document upload, reliability, and data-layer questions.
Ambiguous prompts currently fall back safely in four cases, but Sprint 5 should add clarification behaviour for a full pass.
The Sprint 3 retrieval defaults remain unchanged until the team reruns the corpus against live ChromaDB-backed retrieval and generation.
